title: fix(auth): reject terminal stdin for --with-token

labels.name: external
labels.description: pull request originating outside of the CLI core team

body:

<!-- List related issues here. Use `fixes` or `closes` keywords to associate an issue number. -->
Fixes #9789

### Description

<!--
What's the problem? How are we addressing it?

Write for a reviewer who has not worked in this part of the codebase. Give them the
background they need before the problem makes sense, and avoid jargon.
-->

`gh auth login --with-token` reads the token from standard input with `io.ReadAll`, which
returns only when the input stream ends. If standard input is the terminal, that end never
arrives: the command prints nothing and waits indefinitely, so it looks like it hung. The
flag's own example, `gh auth login --with-token < mytoken.txt`, is the form that works, and
the terminal case is a misuse of the flag rather than a flow the command supports.

This change rejects that case before anything is read. In `NewCmdLogin`'s `RunE`, after the
existing `--web` and `--scopes` exclusivity checks, combining `--with-token` with
`opts.IO.IsStdinTTY()` now returns a `cmdutil.FlagErrorf` naming the piped form. Because it
is a flag error, gh prints the usage block beside it, so the correct invocation is on screen
at the moment the mistake is reported:

```console
$ gh auth login --with-token
argument to `--with-token` must be piped in through standard input, for example `gh auth login --with-token < mytoken.txt`

Usage:  gh auth login [flags]

Flags:
  -w, --web                   Open a browser to authenticate
      --with-token            Read token from standard input
  ...
```

Piped and redirected input are unchanged: `io.ReadAll` consumes standard input exactly as
before, including the empty-input case that falls through to the existing non-interactive
path. The two table cases in `Test_NewCmdLogin` that asserted a token could be read from a
terminal now assert the error, and `Test_NewCmdLogin_withTokenStdin` covers the message, the
flag-error type, that the run function is never reached, and both non-terminal shapes.

### How did you test this change?

<!--
Report only actions you actually performed and results you actually observed, using factual
first-person language (for example, "I ran..." and "I saw..."). Do not present planned,
hypothetical, inferred, or merely expected scenarios as testing.

Automated test results do not belong here. Passing unit tests, `go test ./...` output, and
coverage numbers tell a reviewer nothing they cannot see from CI, so do not paste them.

If you did not exercise the changed behavior, write `Not tested` and explain why.

Use one or more of these, whichever communicates best:

1. Screenshots or GIFs of the real command running. Preferred whenever the change is visible
   in terminal output. If output changed, show it before and after.
2. Given/When/Then scenarios, but only when you actually executed the steps. For example:
   Given I was in a repo with no open pull requests
   When I ran `gh pr list`
   Then I saw "no open pull requests in cli/cli"
3. A natural language walkthrough of what you did by hand, the states you covered, and what
   you saw, including error and edge cases.

If you leave this empty, your pull request will very likely be closed.
-->

I built with `make` and ran `bin/gh` from this checkout each time, never an installed gh. For
the terminal cases I allocated a real pseudo-terminal with `/usr/bin/script -q /dev/null`, so
standard input was genuinely a terminal rather than a value I asserted in a test. I isolated
authentication state in a throwaway `GH_CONFIG_DIR` and unset `GH_TOKEN` and `GITHUB_TOKEN`,
so nothing in my existing configuration was read or written.

1. Given the binary from this branch
   When I ran `gh auth login --with-token` with standard input on a terminal
   Then I saw the new error followed by the `gh auth login` usage block, and the process
   exited right away.

2. Given the binary from this branch
   When I ran `printf 'abc123\n' | gh auth login --with-token`
   Then I saw `error validating token: HTTP 401: Bad credentials (https://api.github.com/)`,
   which is the unchanged outcome: the token came off the pipe and went to validation.

3. Given a binary I built from trunk with both files reverted
   When I ran `gh auth login --with-token` with standard input on a terminal
   Then I saw no output after 12 seconds and `pgrep` still listed the process, confirming it
   was blocked on standard input. I killed it.

4. Given the binary from this branch
   When I ran `gh auth login --web --with-token` with standard input on a terminal
   Then I saw `specify only one of `--web` or `--with-token``, so the pre-existing conflict
   check still wins over the new one.

I saw no credential written anywhere during these runs: the config file and `hosts.yml` under
my real `~/.config/gh` kept their existing modification times.

One thing I could not provide: the preferred evidence form here is a GIF of the command
running, and VHS, ttyd, and ffmpeg are not installed on this machine, so the observations
above are prose.

### Key points

<!--
Tradeoffs you accepted, alternatives you rejected, and anything a reviewer would otherwise have to guess at.
-->

- The condition is `IsStdinTTY()`, not `CanPrompt()`. `CanPrompt()` also requires stdout to be
  a terminal, but the block depends on stdin alone: `gh auth login --with-token | tee log`
  leaves a terminal on stdin and still hangs, so keying off stdin catches a case the broader
  helper would miss.
- A flag error, not a plain error, so gh prints the usage block with its examples. This
  matches how the adjacent `--web` and `--scopes` rejections already behave.
- I rejected prompting for the token in the terminal. #9789 states the team does not want
  credential prompts there, and it would reach well past the acceptance criteria.
- Landing order matters here. #14452 adds `if tokenStdin && opts.ShortLived` in the same
  `RunE` block and edits the same test file, so whichever of the two lands second needs a
  rebase. I raise it because it is a review-ordering question a reviewer would otherwise have
  to discover, not because this diff depends on that one.

### Notes for reviewers

<!--
Where should review start, and what should be read next? Call out anything you are unsure about.

Link related issues or prior discussion, with one sentence on why each matters.
-->

Start with the six added lines in `NewCmdLogin` in `pkg/cmd/auth/login/login.go`; the rest of
the diff is tests.

- #9789 carries the acceptance criteria this implements, including the framing that the fix is
  an error rather than an added prompt.
- #14452 touches the same statements in the same function and the same test file, which is why
  it appears under Key points.
